title: The curse of the Fall and the promise of a Redeemer
summary: At the Fall God foretold a descendant of the woman who would be wounded yet would deal the serpent a fatal blow. Johnson reads it as a single event fulfilled at the Messiah's death in AD 32; it is listed here as given at Creation.

title: Cain will be a vagabond
summary: After Abel's murder God said the soil would not yield to Cain and he would be a restless wanderer, though protected by a mark. Cain left for the land of Nod and lived unsettled before founding a city named for his son. Year estimated from Seth's birth at 130 AM.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History (AM chronology table)

title: Adam will die if he eats of the Tree of Knowledge
summary: God warned that eating the forbidden fruit would bring death. Johnson explains that the dying process began at the Fall and ended when Adam died at 930 years (930 AM).

title: Flood will destroy the earth if mankind does not repent within 120 years
summary: God gave humanity 120 years before judgment. Johnson dates the warning to 2388 BC and the Flood to 2268 BC on the 17th day of the second month, exactly 120 years later.

sources.name: Grace thru Faith: How long did Noah preach?

title: Adam predicts worldwide destructions by fire and water
summary: Josephus records that Adam predicted two universal judgments, one by water and one by fire; Johnson adds Jasher's note that Cainan inscribed this on stone tablets. The water judgment came with the Flood; the fire judgment is still future.

title: Canaanites will become slaves to Shem
summary: Noah cursed Canaan to servitude under his brothers. When Israel (of Shem) conquered Canaan, the Gibeonites became bondservants and other Canaanites were put to forced labour. Johnson also reads the passage as the God of Shem dwelling in Shem's line.

title: Confusion of languages will occur – Tower of Babel
summary: God said He would confuse the builders' language so they could not understand one another. The work stopped and the peoples were scattered across the earth; Johnson dates this to 1931 BC.

title: Barren Sarah will conceive Isaac
summary: God promised that Sarah, ninety and long barren, would bear Abraham a son. She conceived and gave birth to Isaac.

title: Sodom and Gomorrah will be destroyed
summary: God told Abraham He would judge Sodom and Gomorrah, and the angels told Lot the city would be destroyed. Fire and brimstone fell that same year; Johnson places the ruins under the Dead Sea. (His table prints 1876 for this row; the alignment is uncertain.)

title: Isaac will be born on the exact day prophesied
summary: God named the exact season, "at this set time next year", for Isaac's birth. Johnson notes Isaac was born on the very day appointed.

title: Abraham will become the father of many nations
summary: God renamed Abram as father of a multitude of nations. Through Isaac, Ishmael and Keturah's sons came Israel, Edom (with its early kings), the Ishmaelite tribes and Midian.

title: Ishmael will be a wild man and beget 12 nations
summary: God said Ishmael would be untamed, live alongside his brothers and father twelve princes. Genesis lists his twelve sons as tribal chiefs settled from Havilah to Shur.

title: Ishmael will become a great nation
summary: When Hagar and Ishmael were sent away, God promised to make the boy a great nation. His descendants became the Ishmaelite tribes, which Johnson links to the Arab peoples.

title: God tells Joseph in a dream that he will rule over his family
summary: At seventeen Joseph dreamed of sheaves and of the sun, moon and eleven stars bowing to him. After he was sold into slavery and rose to rule Egypt, his brothers came to buy grain and bowed before him.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History (AM chronology table)

title: Joseph interprets pharaoh's dream of a seven-year famine
summary: Joseph interpreted Pharaoh's dreams of cows and ears of grain as seven abundant years followed by seven years of famine. Both came as foretold, and Joseph was made ruler over Egypt. (Johnson's table shows 1698 near this row; the given year here is worked back from his 1686 BC anchor.)

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History (AM chronology table)

title: Jacob will be in Egypt with Joseph before he dies
summary: At Beersheba God told Jacob not to fear going to Egypt. Jacob went down and was reunited with Joseph in Goshen.

title: Joseph will be with Jacob when Jacob dies
summary: God promised that Joseph would put his hand on Jacob's eyes. Seventeen years later Jacob died with Joseph beside him, who mourned and embalmed him.

title: Abraham will be blessed by becoming a great nation
summary: God called the childless Abram at age 75 and promised to make him a great nation. His descendants left Egypt as a people of some 600,000 men. Given year from Abraham's birth in 1948 AM.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History (AM chronology table)

title: Abraham's great nation will inherit all the land of Canaan
summary: God showed Abram the land in every direction and promised it to his seed. Under Joshua Israel took possession and the land was divided by tribe; Scripture notes that none of the promises failed.

title: The great nation will come through the seed of Isaac
summary: God said His covenant would be established with Isaac and that Abraham's seed would be called through him. God renewed the promises to Isaac, and the nation that left Egypt descended from him.

title: The great nation will come through Jacob/Israel and his descendants
summary: God passed the Abrahamic promise of land and countless seed to Jacob. His twelve sons became the tribes of Israel that left Egypt as a nation.

title: The great nation, Israel, will be enslaved
summary: In the covenant between the pieces God told Abram his descendants would be sojourners and be enslaved and afflicted. After Joseph's generation died a new Pharaoh forced Israel into hard bondage. Given year is Johnson's 2018 AM covenant.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History (AM chronology table)

title: God will send plagues on Egypt to force pharaoh to let the Israelites go
summary: God promised to stretch out His hand and strike Egypt with wonders, after which Pharaoh would release Israel. Ten plagues followed and Israel was driven out.

title: Israel will leave Egypt with spoil
summary: God promised the enslaved nation would come out with great substance, and told Moses they would not leave empty-handed. The Egyptians gave Israel silver, gold and clothing as they departed.

title: Israel will return to the land of Canaan (Israel)
summary: God said Abram's descendants would return once the Amorites' iniquity was complete. Israel crossed the Jordan into Canaan under Joshua in 1436 BC.

title: Israel will be blessed and become numerous
summary: God promised Abram countless descendants and blessing. By the Exodus Israel had multiplied greatly, and Moses told them they were as the stars of heaven for multitude.

title: Abraham's descendants will be brought out of captivity after 430 years
summary: God foretold a long sojourn and deliverance. Johnson counts 430 years from the covenant (2018 AM) to the Exodus (2448 AM), ending on the very day as Exodus 12:41 states; his Onah table places it on Nisan 15.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History (AM chronology table)

title: Jews will always keep the Passover
summary: God ordained Passover to be kept forever, including in the land He would give. Israel kept it at Gilgal on entering Canaan, and Jews have kept it ever since, as Johnson notes.

title: Israel will wander in the desert for 40 years
summary: After the spies' report God decreed a year of wandering for each of the forty days, until all counted men over twenty died, while their children entered. Johnson cites the Seder Olam that Israel entered Canaan forty years to the day.

title: Jericho will be destroyed
summary: God told Joshua to circle Jericho for six days and seven times on the seventh, and the wall would collapse. On the seventh day at the shout the wall fell flat and the city was taken.

title: Eli's sons will be cursed
summary: A man of God told Eli his house would be judged and gave a sign: both his sons would die the same day. When the Philistines captured the ark both were killed in the battle.

title: A Benjamite, Saul, will be the first king
summary: God told Samuel that the next day a man from Benjamin would come whom he should anoint. Saul arrived searching for donkeys, was anointed, and later chosen by lot.

title: Samuel predicts Saul will lose the kingdom
summary: After Saul spared Agag, Samuel declared God had rejected him and torn the kingdom away for someone better. The kingdom passed to David.

title: David will be king
summary: Samuel anointed the shepherd boy David among his brothers and the Spirit came on him. David became king over Judah at Hebron and later over all Israel; Johnson dates his accession to 1040 BC.

title: Saul and his sons will die
summary: At Endor Saul was told that Israel would fall to the Philistines and that he and his sons would die the next day. Saul and three sons died on Mount Gilboa.

title: David's sin will cause his child to die
summary: Nathan told David that although his sin was forgiven the child would die. The baby fell ill and died on the seventh day.

title: David's sin will cause constant violence in his house
summary: Nathan said violence would plague David's family and a close relative would take his wives publicly. Amnon was murdered, Absalom rebelled and lay with David's concubines on the roof, and Absalom was killed.

title: David's throne will continue forever
summary: God promised David a descendant whose throne would last forever. Jesus was born of David's line and announced as heir to David's throne. His visible reign is still future. This is #38 in Johnson's book.

title: Solomon will take the throne and build the Temple
summary: David's son, not David, would build God's house. Solomon began the Temple in his fourth year, 480 years after the Exodus; Johnson dates this to 989 BC (his later anchors give foundation 2928 AM, dedication 2935 AM).

sources.name: Ken Johnson, AM anchors (dsscalendar.org Onah intro: Temple 2935 AM, destroyed 3338 AM)

title: Priestly lineage from Eli will be destroyed
summary: A man of God told Eli his house would lose the priesthood and a faithful priest would replace it. Solomon removed Abiathar, Eli's descendant, and installed Zadok, 'that he might fulfil the word of the LORD'.

title: Prophet Iddo will be killed for disobedience
summary: The man of God who cried against Bethel's altar was told he would not be buried with his fathers for eating in Bethel against God's command. A lion killed him on the road. (Johnson's book names him Iddo, after Jewish tradition.)

title: Jeroboam's dynasty will be destroyed
summary: Ahijah said God would sweep away Jeroboam's house. Baasha killed Jeroboam's son Nadab and wiped out the whole family, 'according to the saying of the LORD'.

title: Jehu predicts Baasha's dynasty will be destroyed
summary: Jehu son of Hanani warned that Baasha's house would end like Jeroboam's. Zimri killed Baasha's son Elah and every male of the family.

title: Elijah predicts a drought will occur in Israel (3-year drought, 890-887 BC)
summary: Elijah announced a drought that would end only at his word. It lasted about three and a half years, until rain came after the contest on Carmel.

title: The meal and oil of the widow will not fail
summary: Elijah promised the widow of Zarephath that her jar of flour and jug of oil would last until the rain returned. They did not run out.

title: Ahab to have victory over Syria
summary: A prophet told Ahab that God would hand Ben-Hadad's great army over to him through the young men of the provinces. Israel routed the Syrians.

title: Ruins of cursed Jericho will be rebuilt
summary: Joshua cursed anyone who rebuilt Jericho. Hiel lost his eldest and youngest sons when he rebuilt it under Ahab. 4Q175 ends with this curse and, quoting the Psalms of Joshua (4Q379), applies it again to a wicked man of its own day who rebuilt the city.

title: Ahab/Israel will suffer because of sparing Ben-Hadad
summary: Because Ahab released Ben-Hadad, whom God had doomed, a prophet said Ahab's life would go for his. Ahab was later killed fighting the Syrians at Ramoth-gilead.

title: Micaiah predicts Ahab & Jehoshaphat will be defeated
Ahab will die and dogs will lick up his blood
summary: After Naboth's murder, Elijah told Ahab that dogs would lick his blood. When Ahab's chariot was washed at the pool of Samaria, the dogs licked up his blood.

title: Jezebel will be eaten by dogs
summary: Elijah said dogs would eat Jezebel at Jezreel. When Jehu took power she was thrown from a window, and only her skull, feet and palms were left to bury.

title: Elijah predicts Ahaziah I will die because of consulting Baal-Zebub
summary: Ahaziah, injured in a fall, sent to ask the god of Ekron whether he would recover. Elijah said he would never leave his bed, and he died.

title: Elijah will be taken to heaven on a certain day
summary: The prophets at Bethel and Jericho knew God would take Elijah that day. A chariot of fire parted Elijah and Elisha, and Elijah went up in a whirlwind.

title: Elijah predicts Elisha will receive a double portion of Elijah's spirit
summary: Elijah said Elisha would have his request if he saw Elijah taken. Elisha saw it, parted the Jordan with Elijah's mantle, and the prophets said Elijah's spirit rested on him.

title: Elisha predicts the Moabites will be conquered through a miracle of water
Elisha predicts Naaman will be healed if Naaman obeys him
Moab, Ammon, & Edom will be destroyed without Judah fighting them
summary: Jahaziel told Jehoshaphat the battle was God's and Judah would only have to stand and watch. The invaders turned on one another and none escaped.

title: Elisha predicts his servant, Gehazi, will become leprous because of greed
A seven-year famine predicted (881-875 BC)
summary: Elisha warned the Shunammite woman that God had called for a seven-year famine. She lived in Philistia for seven years and on her return got her land back.

title: Elisha predicts Hazael will become king of Aram
summary: Elisha told Hazael that God had shown him Hazael would be king of Syria. The next day Hazael smothered Ben-Hadad and took the throne.

title: Jehu will become king of Israel
summary: Elijah was told at Horeb to anoint Jehu king over Israel. Elisha's servant anointed him, and Jehu overthrew Joram and took the throne.

title: Elijah predicts Jehoram will die of a disease & his family taken captive
summary: A letter from Elijah told Jehoram that his household would be plundered and he would die of a lingering bowel disease. Philistines and Arabs carried off his family, and he died in agony two years later.

title: Elisha predicted Israel will defeat Aram three times
summary: The dying Elisha had Joash strike the ground with arrows; he stopped at three, so he would beat Syria only three times. Joash beat Ben-Hadad three times and recovered Israel's cities.

title: God will abandon Joash because he killed the prophet Zechariah
summary: Zechariah warned that because Judah had forsaken God, God had forsaken them; dying, he asked God to see and require it. A small Syrian force defeated Judah, and Joash was murdered by his servants.

title: Amaziah will be killed because of sin
summary: A prophet told Amaziah that God had decided to destroy him for worshipping the gods of conquered Edom. Israel defeated him, and conspirators later killed him at Lachish.

title: Jehu's descendants will sit on the throne for four generations
summary: Jehu was promised descendants on Israel's throne to the fourth generation. Jehoahaz, Joash, Jeroboam II and Zechariah reigned; Shallum killed Zechariah, 'the word of the LORD which he spake unto Jehu'.

title: Jonah warns the Assyrians of destruction
summary: Jonah announced that Nineveh would be overthrown in forty days. The city repented and was spared then; Johnson notes its sin came back, and Babylon destroyed it later (612 BC).

title: Moab will be captured by Assyria within three years of this prophecy
Moab and Edom will be destroyed
summary: Balaam foresaw a ruler from Jacob who would strike Moab and possess Edom. David first subdued both, and Johnson lists their later ruin in the Assyrian period; many read the star as finally the Messiah.

title: Kenites will be taken captive by Assyria
summary: Balaam said the Kenites, safe in their rocky nest, would be wasted until Assyria carried them captive. Johnson places this in the Assyrian deportations of about 722 BC.

title: Arabia will fall to Assyria
fulfilment: Sargon II's campaign against the Arab tribes
summary: Isaiah said that within a year all the glory of Kedar would fail and few of its archers would remain. Johnson dates Arabia's fall to Assyria to 715 BC.

title: Assyria will besiege Jerusalem (185,000 Assyrians died)
summary: Isaiah said the king of Assyria would not enter Jerusalem, shoot an arrow there or build a siege mound. The angel of the LORD struck 185,000 in the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib went home.

title: Sennacherib will be assassinated
Shebna will die because of disrespect
summary: Isaiah said Shebna, the proud steward carving his own tomb, would be thrown out and Eliakim given his office and key. During the Assyrian crisis Eliakim is over the household and Shebna is only scribe.

title: Amalekites' final destruction predicted
summary: God swore war on Amalek until its memory was blotted out, and Balaam said its end would be destruction. In Hezekiah's days Simeonites struck the last Amalekites who had escaped, and Amalek vanishes from history.

title: Hezekiah will live another 15 years (711-696 BC)
summary: Isaiah first told the dying Hezekiah to set his house in order, then returned to say God would heal him, add fifteen years and defend the city. Hezekiah recovered and reigned until 696 BC in Johnson's count.

title: Manasseh's downfall predicted
summary: The prophets told Manasseh that God would bring such evil on Jerusalem that ears would tingle. Johnson dates Manasseh's downfall to 641 BC (he was also taken to Babylon in hooks); the full judgment on the city came in 587 BC.

title: A man named Josiah will arise and destroy the idolaters
summary: About three centuries ahead, a man of God named Josiah of David's line as the king who would burn the priests' bones on Jeroboam's altar. Josiah tore down the Bethel altar and burned bones from the tombs on it.

sources.name: David Guzik (Calvary Chapel), Enduring Word, 1 Kings 13

title: Nineveh (Assyria) will be permanently destroyed
summary: Nahum said Nineveh would be finished with an overrunning flood and its river gates opened and palace dissolved. The Medes and Babylonians took the city in 612 BC; ancient writers say a flood broke down part of the wall.

sources.name: Fall of Nineveh (Wikipedia; Babylonian Chronicle ABC 3)

title: Assyrians will be drunk the night of the Babylonian attack
Ninevites will be completely wiped out
Nineveh's fortresses will be easily captured
Nineveh will be destroyed by fire
summary: Nahum said Nineveh's gates would be thrown open and fire would consume its bars and the city. Excavations show the city was burned in its fall.

sources.name: Fall of Nineveh (Wikipedia; Babylonian Chronicle ABC 3)

title: 70-year Babylonian captivity will begin
Judah will be taken captive to Babylon because of idolatry
After three Babylonian rulers, Persian Empire will take over
Babylonian King Nebuchadnezzar will go insane for seven years (582-575 BC)
The kingdom of Lydia will fall to the Persians
fulfilment: Persian conquests of Lydia (547), Babylon (539) and Egypt (525 BC)
summary: Daniel's second beast, a bear raised on one side with three ribs in its mouth, is read as Medo-Persia, with Persia the stronger side. Its three great conquests were Lydia, Babylon and Egypt.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Daniel 11 Time Map (Persia 536-326 BC; Cambyses takes Egypt 525 BC; Xerxes I 486-465 BC)

title: After 70 years, the Babylonian captivity will end
Babylon will fall to the Medes and Persians
summary: More than 150 years ahead, while Babylon was an Assyrian province, Isaiah named the Medes as the ones God would stir up against it. The Medes and Persians took Babylon in 539 BC.

sources.name: Fall of Babylon (Wikipedia; Nabonidus Chronicle, 16 Tashritu = 12 Oct 539 BC)
David Guzik (Calvary Chapel), Enduring Word, Daniel 5 (gates; Isaiah 44:28-45:7; Jeremiah 51:57-58)

title: Cyrus will take Babylon (gates will be open before Cyrus)
summary: Isaiah said God would open double doors before Cyrus so the gates would not be shut, and loosen the loins of kings. Herodotus says the river gates of Babylon were left open the night the Persians entered.

sources.name: David Guzik (Calvary Chapel), Enduring Word, Daniel 5 (gates; Isaiah 44:28-45:7; Jeremiah 51:57-58)
Chuck Smith, Through the Bible C2000, Isaiah 41 (Cyrus named c. 150 years ahead)
Fall of Babylon (Wikipedia; Nabonidus Chronicle, 16 Tashritu = 12 Oct 539 BC)

title: Cyrus will free the Jews (Josephus Ant. 11:1)
summary: Isaiah named Cyrus as God's shepherd, the one who would say of Jerusalem 'it shall be built' and of the Temple 'its foundation shall be laid'. About 150 years later Cyrus issued the decree to rebuild the Temple.

sources.name: Chuck Smith, Through the Bible C2000, Isaiah 41 (Cyrus named c. 150 years ahead)
David Guzik (Calvary Chapel), Enduring Word, Daniel 5 (gates; Isaiah 44:28-45:7; Jeremiah 51:57-58)

title: Israel and Judah will come back as one nation from Assyria and Babylon
Temple vessels will be restored
summary: Contradicting prophets who promised a quick return of the vessels, Jeremiah said the rest would also go to Babylon and stay until God visited them, then come back. Cyrus gave Sheshbazzar 5,400 gold and silver vessels to take home.

title: Kingdom of Egypt will fall to the Persians
After four kings, Persian Empire will attack Greece (537-465 BC)
Ezra will restore the Temple services
Alexander the Great will conquer the known world
summary: After the Persian kings a mighty king would rise and do as he pleased. Johnson's map gives Alexander 326-323 BC (secular reign 336-323 BC).

title: Tyre will be destroyed
Ekron will be destroyed, never to rise again
summary: Zechariah announces the word of the LORD against the Syrian cities of Hadrach, Damascus and Hamath. After Issus, Alexander's forces took Damascus and the Syrian interior.

title: Ashkalon and Gaza will be destroyed
Ashdod will be taken over
God will protect Jerusalem from Alexander's army
Alexander's empire will be split into four smaller empires
summary: As soon as he stood up, his kingdom would be broken. Alexander died at 32, only a few years after reaching full power.

title: Ptolemy I Soter will help Seleucus Nicator retake Syria (323-285 BC)
fulfilment: History: Ptolemy I and Seleucus I
summary: The king of the South (Ptolemy I of Egypt) would be strong, but one of his commanders would become stronger. Seleucus, once Ptolemy's officer, built the larger Seleucid kingdom. Johnson's dates: Ptolemy I 323-285 BC, Seleucus 311-280 BC.

title: Berenice will marry Antiochus II (~285-246 BC)
summary: A daughter of the southern king would marry the northern king to seal an alliance, but she would not keep her position. Berenice married Antiochus II. After his death Laodice had her and her son killed, as Seleucus II took the throne (Johnson: 246 BC).

title: Berenice and Antiochus will be poisoned
Ptolemy II will die
Ptolemy III will avenge Berenice's death by killing Laodice
fulfilment: History: Third Syrian War, Ptolemy III
summary: One from her family line would attack the northern king's fortress and prevail. Her brother Ptolemy III Euergetes invaded Seleucid territory to avenge her (Johnson: 246-221 BC).

title: Ptolemy will take Syrian and Egyptian idols back home
fulfilment: History: Canopus Decree records returned idols
summary: The southern king would carry off their gods, images and treasures to Egypt. Ptolemy III brought back statues the Persians had taken. Johnson's footnote ties these to Cambyses' plunder of 525 BC.

title: Seleucus III and Antiochus III will attack Egypt at the "battle of Raphia"
fulfilment: History: Seleucus III and Antiochus III
summary: His sons would gather great forces and sweep through to the southern fortress. Seleucus III and then Antiochus III went to war, and Antiochus advanced to Raphia (Johnson: by 218 BC).

title: Antiochus III will attack Egypt
summary: The northern king would return years later with a larger army and great riches. When Ptolemy IV died, Antiochus III attacked his child heir (Johnson: about 13 years after 217 BC).

title: False Prophet will arise and mislead many
summary: Many would rise against the southern king, and lawless men among the Jews would try to fulfil the vision but fall. Philip V allied with Antiochus III, and some Jews sided with Antiochus. The Egyptian general Scopas crushed the revolt.

title: Antiochus III will gain complete control of Israel
summary: The northern king would do as he pleased and stand in the Beautiful Land. Judea passed from Ptolemaic to Seleucid control (Johnson: by 197 BC).

title: Cleopatra I will marry Ptolemy V
fulfilment: History: Cleopatra I marries Ptolemy V
summary: He would give a daughter in marriage to undermine the kingdom, but she would not serve his plan. Antiochus III married Cleopatra I to Ptolemy V, and she sided with her husband (Johnson: 194 BC).

title: Battle of Magnesia will occur
fulfilment: History: Lucius Scipio defeats Antiochus III
summary: He would turn to the coastlands and take many, but a commander would stop him and turn his scorn back on him. Rome under Scipio Asiaticus defeated Antiochus at Magnesia.

title: Seleucus IV will order an attack on the Jerusalem Temple
summary: His successor would send a tax collector through the glorious kingdom and then die, not in anger or battle. Seleucus IV sent Heliodorus to seize the Temple treasury and was later poisoned by him (Johnson: 187-175 BC).

title: Antiochus Epiphanes will rise to power
summary: A despised man without rightful claim would take the throne by intrigue. Antiochus IV pushed aside the heir Demetrius I (Johnson: reigned 175-164 BC).

title: Antiochus Epiphanes will assassinate Onias
summary: Armies would be swept away before him, and the prince of the covenant would be broken. Johnson identifies this prince as the deposed high priest Onias III, who was murdered.

title: Antiochus Epiphanes will deceive Rome into officially recognizing him
summary: After making alliances he would act deceitfully and hand out plunder as his fathers never did. Johnson says Antiochus deceived Rome into recognising him. Ancient writers note his lavish handouts.

title: Maccabees will revolt against Greek-ruled Syria
summary: Those who knew their God would stand firm and act. Mattathias and Judas Maccabeus led the revolt and retook the Temple (Johnson: Maccabean era 164-64 BC).

title: Grecian Empire will fall to Rome
Rome will destroy Ashur (Syria/Assyria)
summary: Isaiah gave the sign of a virgin bearing a son. Matthew and Luke record Jesus conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: The Messiah will be the One who has existed from eternity
summary: Micah named little Bethlehem as birthplace of Israel's ruler. Jesus was born there, and the scribes quoted this verse to Herod. Johnson dates the birth to 2 BC.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: The Messiah is the preexistent Son of God
The Messiah is God
summary: Isaiah foresaw a child with divine titles who would sit on David's throne forever. The Gospels present Jesus as the incarnate Son. His unending government is still to be fully seen.

title: The only begotten Son of God will be called the Messiah
The Messiah will incarnate into human form (lower than the angels)
The Messiah is both God and Man
summary: God would raise a righteous Branch for David who would reign and be called the LORD our Righteousness. The New Testament presents Jesus as this Son of David. His reign over the land is still future.

title: The Messiah will be called "The mighty God, the everlasting Father"
The Messiah will be called Immanuel, "God with us"
summary: The child would be called Immanuel, 'God with us'. Matthew applies the title to Jesus at his birth.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: The Messiah will be a descendant of Eve
summary: God promised that a descendant of the woman would crush the serpent while being wounded himself. Christians see this begun at the cross and finished at Satan's final defeat. This is #1 in Johnson's book.

title: The Messiah will be a descendant of Shem
The Messiah will be a descendant of Abraham
summary: God promised that through Abraham's offspring all nations would be blessed. Paul says this singular Seed is Christ, a descendant of Abraham.

title: The Messiah will be a descendant of Isaac
The Messiah will be from the tribe of Judah (Shiloh)
summary: Jacob gave the sceptre to Judah. Jesus was born in the tribe of Judah.

title: Jewish kings will not cease until the First Coming of the Messiah
summary: Jacob promised that rule would stay with Judah until Shiloh came. 4Q252 explains that the ruler's staff will not depart until the 'Messiah of Righteousness, the Branch of David' comes, so it read Shiloh as the Messiah. Johnson's book lists it under the Messiah's first coming: Jewish rulers lasted until the Messiah came.

sources.name: Pesher on Genesis / 4Q252 (Wikipedia; manuscript early Herodian)
Wise, Abegg & Cook, The Dead Sea Scrolls: A New Translation, 4Q252 col. 5

title: The Messiah will be a descendant of David
The Messiah will be heir to the throne of David
The Messiah will not be from Jeconiah's lineage (virgin born)
The Messiah will be born of a virgin
summary: A sign for the house of David: a virgin will bear a son called Immanuel, 'God with us'. The verse stands in the pre-Christian Great Isaiah Scroll. Johnson lists it among his 'inscription' prophecies, fulfilled in Jesus' birth in 2 BC. Ken Johnson's New Covenant of Damascus says the Essenes expected a virgin-born Messiah.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The New Covenant of Damascus (description)

title: Gabriel predicts the birth of Jesus while Mary was still a virgin
Jesus will be conceived by the Holy Spirit
summary: An angel told Joseph that Mary's child was from the Holy Spirit and was to be named Jesus. Joseph took Mary as his wife and named the child Jesus.

title: The Messiah will be holy

given.label: 536 BC (1st year of Darius the Mede)

summary: The seventy weeks would end sin, atone for iniquity and bring in everlasting righteousness. Atonement was made at the cross. Johnson holds the 70th week is a future seven-year Tribulation after a gap.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's seventy weeks chapter)

title: The Messiah's name will be Jesus/Joshua
Angel Gabriel predicts John the Baptist's birth to Zachariah
Elisabeth predicts Jesus' birth and Mary's future honor
Zachariah will not speak until John's birth
summary: Because he doubted, Zacharias would be unable to speak until the birth. His speech came back the moment he wrote 'His name is John'.

title: Zachariah's prophetic song
Mary will be a prophetess
Child of the prophetess will be called Mahr-Shalal-Hash-Baz
summary: The Servant would be despised, rejected and held in low esteem. Jesus' own people and leaders rejected him. Chuck Smith ties this to Jesus' rejection.

title: Mary predicts her blessedness and Jesus' rule

summary: Johnson has a 1949 entry for the return of the Yemenite Jews. Operation Magic Carpet airlifted about 49,000 of them, many of whom recalled the promise of "eagles' wings". The prophecy reference here is inferred.

title: There will be constant planting and reaping (crops)
Forests will reappear in Israel (cedar, etc)
Desolate land and cities will be restored
Five cities will stay desolate
Muslims will not "reckon Israel among nations"
Israel will inherit remnant of Edom/Palestinians
Satellite-Television Communication Systems Invented
Sanhedrin will be reestablished
Palestinians will want Jerusalem as their capital
Gaza will be forsaken
summary: Johnson ends his Ashdod–Ashkelon–Gaza entry in 2005 and, in The Rapture, names the handover of Gaza as an event before the Rapture. Israel's withdrawal from Gaza was completed on 12 September 2005.

title: Russia and Iran will sign a military defense pact
Second Lebanese War will occur
An independent state will be created out of the West Bank
summary: Johnson lists, as future after 2008, a sovereign Palestinian state on the West Bank. The reference here is inferred (Joel's rebuke of nations that "parted my land").

title: Fourth Shepherd's Syrian war will occur
Fifth Shepherd's Syrian war will occur
Lebanon-Jordan war will occur
summary: Johnson foresees a "Lebanese-Jordanian" war before the Tribulation. Many prophecy teachers link this to the Psalm 83 coalition of Israel's near neighbours. The reference here is inferred.

title: Sephardic Jews will return to Israel and populate the Negev
Sixth Shepherd's Syrian war will occur
Damascus will be destroyed
summary: Isaiah says Damascus will cease to be a city. Johnson and many prophecy teachers treat this as still future, since Damascus has never been wiped out completely.

title: Gog-Magog War will occur immediately after Israel wins another war
summary: Gog of Magog leads a northern coalition against a regathered Israel living securely, and God destroys it on the mountains of Israel. Johnson calls this the first Gog-Magog war, distinct from the one after the Millennium. Chuck Smith identified Magog as Russia, with Persia, Ethiopia, Libya, Gomer and Togarmah. He expected it in the latter days and thought it might coincide with the Rapture.

sources.name: Chuck Smith, Through the Bible (C2000), Ezekiel 38

title: Rise of the ten nations occurs after the Gog-Magog War
Increased understanding of prophecies will occur
Children will be rebellious and society will be materialistic
Jesus' words will never be forgotten
Christians will be hated for Jesus' Name's sake
The apostasy of the church will fully form
prophecy: 2 Thess. 2:3 (see the book's section on the Apostasy of the Church)
summary: The lawless one is revealed once the restrainer is taken out of the way. Johnson places his revealing at the start of the seven years, which begins the Day of the Lord.

title: The Rapture of the believing church will occur
prophecy: 1 Thess. 4:15-18 (see the book's section on the Rapture)

title: Many false Christs will come
Wars and rumors of wars will occur
Famines, earthquakes, pestilences will occur
Plagues will be widespread
Fearful events and signs from heaven will be seen
Religious persecution will occur
Discord among churches
The falling away will occur
False prophets will arise
Lawlessness will increase
The love of many will grow cold
Severe ocean activity will occur – hurricanes
Apostasy comes (see section on the Apostasy of the Church)
Restrainer leaves (see section on the Rapture of the Church)
Antichrist revealed when he ratifies the peace covenant
summary: If the Millennium starts at 6000 AM (March 2075 – March 2076), Johnson notes that the seven-year Tribulation could begin seven years earlier, March 2067 to March 2068. He presents this as speculation.

title: The Tribulation (Daniel's 70th week) begins a seven-year period with a signed peace covenant
summary: Daniel's 70th week is still future in Johnson's view, with the church age as a gap between the 69th and 70th weeks. It opens when the coming prince confirms a covenant for one week. Johnson calls it the Tribulation peace plan.

sources.name: Skip Heitzig, You Can Understand the Book of Revelation (2011), pre-tribulation premillennial

title: New Jerusalem Temple built
summary: Sacrifice has to resume, and a Temple has to stand, for the Antichrist to stop the offering and sit in God's temple. Johnson cites Irenaeus and Origen for a literal Tribulation Temple.

title: Temple Mount divided
Gospel preached to all nations
Elijah returns and preaches against the Antichrist for 3.5 years
summary: Two witnesses prophesy in Jerusalem for 1,260 days, are killed, lie in the street and rise again. Johnson identifies one as Elijah, whose ministry ends at the sixth trumpet, before the midpoint, as "the restoration of all things".

title: He will be revealed when the ten nations are in power
summary: The fourth beast's ten horns are ten kings who rise before a little horn uproots three of them. Johnson lists the rise of ten nations as a sign before the Tribulation.

title: He will be different from the ten (previous) kings
He will rise to power by trickery like Antiochus Epiphanes did
He will honor those who acknowledge him, make them rulers, and parcel out land for a price
The letters of his name will equal 666 if spelled out in Greek
Antichrist's right eye and one arm damaged
He will subdue three kings (of the ten), then ten kings given into his hand for 42 months
summary: A world ruler speaks great words against God, wears out the saints for 3½ years and claims to be God. The Biblefacts Revelation chart identifies the first seal's white horse with him.

sources.name: Skip Heitzig, You Can Understand the Book of Revelation (2011), pre-tribulation premillennial

title: Egypt, the King of the South, will attack the Antichrist
summary: At the time of the end the king of the south pushes at him, and he overruns countries including Egypt. Johnson places this war in the first half of the Tribulation.

title: Egypt and many other countries will fall to him
Syria, the King of the North, will attack the Antichrist
Many other nations will be destroyed by the Antichrist
He will destroy to an extraordinary degree
He will destroy many while they are at ease (at peace)
The Libyans and Ethiopians will follow at his heels
Rumors from the east and north will disturb him and he will annihilate many
One-fourth of the world's population will be destroyed under his leadership
Animals attack
The remaining seven nations will willingly accept his leadership
He will pitch his royal pavilion between the seas and the holy mountain
He will be a man and the king/ruler of a nation
He will be insolent and skilled in intrigue
His power will be mighty, but not by his own power (demonic power)
He will prosper and perform his will
Through shrewdness, he will cause deceit to succeed
He will magnify himself in his heart
He will do as he pleases
He will fling truth to the ground and perform his will and prosper
He will speak out against the Most High
He will intend to make alterations in the times and laws
He will exalt himself above every known god
He will speak monstrous things against the God of gods
He will show no regard for the god of his fathers
He will worship a strange god that his ancestors never knew
He will honor a strange god of forces
He will not regard the desire of women
He will magnify himself to be equal with the Commander of the Host (Jesus)
He will oppose the Prince of princes
He will deny the Father and Son
He will deny Jesus is the Son of God
He will deny Jesus is the Christ
He will deny Jesus came in the flesh
He will deny Jesus will come back in the flesh
He will take action against the strongest of fortresses with the help of a foreign god
Armies surround Jerusalem
The Jewish people will be expelled from their half of Jerusalem
summary: The kings of the earth are gathered to Armageddon and against Jerusalem, and the returning Christ destroys their armies. Johnson places Armageddon at the end of the seven years, with Christ as the last "shepherd" of Micah 5.

sources.name: Biblefacts.org, Seven Shepherds chart (Ken Johnson ministry)

title: Antichrist's kingdom grows exceedingly great toward the south, east, and toward Israel
He will destroy mighty men and the holy people
He enters the beautiful land and many countries will fall
Jordan will escape out of his hand
He takes his seat in the temple of God, displaying himself as God
He opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or object of worship
God will send upon non-Christians a deluding influence so that they will believe the lie
Antichrist places the Teraphim in the new Temple
He grows in power and causes some of the host to fall
The place of God's sanctuary is thrown down
He removes the regular sacrifice from God
On account of transgression, the host will be given over to the horn along with the regular sacrifice
Peace covenant will be broken
2300 days will start
1290 days will start
summary: In the middle of the week the Antichrist ends the sacrifice and sets up the desolating abomination in the holy place. Johnson takes this as the start of the Great Tribulation, with Daniel's 1,290 days counted from it.

title: 1335 days will start
He will wage war with the saints and overpower them
He will wear down the saints of the Highest One
The saints will be given into his hands for a time, times, and half a time
Antichrist will persecute Messianic Jews
1260 days will start
Some of the Jews will flee to Petra/Bozrah
summary: The dragon is cast down and persecutes the woman, who is fed in a wilderness refuge for 1,260 days. Jesus told those in Judea to flee to the mountains.

title: The sign of the sun and moon going dark will occur
The wrath of God will begin
Days will be shortened
The wrath of God will end
He will be broken without human agency (by Christ)
He will prosper until the indignation is finished (until the Second Coming)
He will be destroyed and thrown into the fire
Jesus will return exactly the way He left
summary: After the sun is darkened, the Son of Man comes on the clouds with power, his feet stand on the Mount of Olives and he destroys the Antichrist. Johnson ties it to Yom Kippur and the Great Trump, and puts the most likely window at AD 2025/26–2075.

sources.name: Skip Heitzig, You Can Understand the Book of Revelation (2011), pre-tribulation premillennial

title: Messiah's feet will land on the Mount of Olives
Mount of Olives will split in two
Jesus will enter into Jerusalem through the Eastern Gate
All nations will gather against Him - Armageddon
They will look upon Him whom they pierced
Israel cleansed of all sin
summary: God pours out a spirit of grace on Jerusalem. They look on him whom they pierced and mourn, and a fountain is opened for cleansing. Paul says that when the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, all Israel will be saved.

title: Times of the Gentiles will be over
1000 year reign established
Temple Mount will be cleansed and the foundation stone laid
New millennial Temple will be dedicated
All nations will receive the pure language of Hebrew
Ancient relics will be brought back
Israel will have new borders
Human lifespan will return to the original length
Last Gog-Magog War
summary: Satan is released, gathers Gog and Magog from the four corners against the camp of the saints, and fire from heaven devours them. Johnson treats this as a separate, final Gog-Magog war at the end of the Millennium.

title: New Heaven and Earth
summary: The first heaven and earth pass away and God makes all things new. In Johnson's 7,000-year scheme this follows the end of the Millennium at 7000 AM.
